newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Norilsk may see lower output on gas cuts.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Norilsk may see lower output on gas cuts.

text.p: A recent cut in gas supplies to Russian Norilsk Nickel's main group of plants may affect production, company officials said on Monday.

"It's not affecting nickel output at the main plant, but it will affect copper output and operations at Nadezhdinsky," said Mikhail Steklov, director of the main nickel plant at the Norilsk mining and metallurgical complex.
He said his facility used relatively little gas and had made up for the lower gas supplies by switching over to heavy fuel oil.

Yuri Sukhabayevsky, director of the Nadezhdinsky metallurgical plant, which produces copper anodes and convertor matte nickel and accounts for about 25 percent of Norilsk's total output of those metals, said the cuts had so far not affected output at his plant but that things could change.
Nadezhdinsky is part of the Norilsk mining and metallurgical complex, the Norilsk's group's flagship group of plants.
Norilskgazprom, the sole supplier of natural gas to Norilsk, said last week it had slashed supplies to 11 million cubic meters a day from 16 million since June 3 over unpaid gas debts.

"Of course this could affect output if it continues," said Anatoly Komrakov, spokesman for Norilsk group. None of the officials contacted could state the extent to which output at Norilsk -- a major world producer of nickel, copper, cobalt and platinum group metals -- might be affected.
